Title: Limited research
Description: Just a simple research. Web searching, AI asking and putting it all together in a dataset.

Title: Customer focus research
Description: Who is your main customer? Who will benefit from your service? How can you deliver a value?

Title: Technical focus research
Description: How to make what you wana make? What technologies would you use? How can they work together?

Title: Full scale research
Description: You throw all your resources and efforts to make your product the best fit possible. It will help in a long run... probably.

Title: Essential prototype
Description: This prototipe will just show that your idea works. It is ugly. It is buggy. But it proves the very basic concept.

Title: Service prototype
Description: This isn't a technical prototype. You have your landing page up and running, and you should do everything else by hand with every client.

Title: Technical prototype
Description: Now you know, that everything is working on the technical side. User experience? Never heard about this.

Title: Product MVP
Description: This MVP proves everything and you can ship it to selected audience. It is well designed. Well built. And it took time and effort to make it this early.

Title: Mission only
Description: Now your crew knows why are you doing what you are doing.

Title: Values and Strategy
Description: Values will help your team to make important decisions. Strategy will navigate them on which decisions they should make.

Title: Values and Mission
Description: Values will help your team to make important decisions. Mission will give them purpose to make these decisions.

Title: Values, Mission and Strategy
Description: You have done it all. Now your team knows why, how, and which decisions they should make. It invokes confidence.

Title: Internal testing
Description: Your team and friends are enough to test your product. There is no need to gather the audience.

Title: Medium focus group testing
Description: Your testing group consists of a few dozens of people both from your audience and new ones. It will help to catch criticals in your product.

Title: Real-world testing
Description: It is relatively good idea to just put your product online and acquire some users to simply use it. If you are ready to rapidly fix all appearing problems.

Title: Cascade testing with user groups
Description: Full-scale testing with several stages, each bigger. You have prepared and made it all

Title: Website building
Description: You definitely need a website. Anything else? Probaply, not.

Title: Social media setup
Description: Who needs a website when you can make it all with a proper social media account?

Title: Website and Social Media
Description: It is often easier to gather audience via social media, but they should be landed somewhere.

Title: Full marketing commitment
Description: Social media, website, community hub, press releases, and contacts with influencers. You should have it all to succeed.

Title: Single server
Description: Simple backand will be more then enough. So why bother and spend additional money on an ifrastructure? What could possibly go wrong?

Title: Cloud infrastructure
Description: Why should we bother to make our own server if we can use a cloud? It is a little bit more expensive, but definitely much more convenient.

Title: Multiple servers
Description: We know how to make it on our own with all the redundancy we need to provide a consistent service to our clients.

Title: DevOPS team with an infrastructure
Description: Infrastructure needs to be carfully planned and maintained. So we need to hire a DevOPS team to help use make this project.

Title: Self application
Description: Just prepare all the documents and send it according to instructions on a DPG website.

Title: Contact DPG office to assist
Description: We can make it with the DPG office, if they are able to help.

Title: Address SDG relevance only
Description: You have checked if your product is SDG relevant or not. If it is - so why bother? It will work anyway.

Title: DPG indicator checklist
Description: You have your checklist, so you go thugh all 9 indicators and prepare properly your application.

Title: Release marketing campaign
Description: Your team is fully focused on a marketing campaign for the release. The technical side of things is not in focus.

Title: Release event
Description: Just throw a release event to attract an audience. They will watch the stream and then they will use your product.

Title: Some release preparations
Description: You clearly have not enough time to make it all, but you can address the majore issues and prepare the campaign on a decent level.

Title: Full scale release preparations
Description: Your team is working on the release, giving attention to everything. It will take time. But since you have one, you can afford it.

Title: Essential support only
Description: We don't have enough resources for the full scale support, so we will do only bare essentials.

Title: Phone and email customer support
Description: We will conduct a customer support via both phone and email.

Title: Support with LiveOPS
Description: We will not only make a support up and running, but also establish regular events and activities for our clients (LiveOPS).

Title: Outsourced support
Description: We no need our team to make a customer support. Let's hire an outsource company to make it for us!

Title: Desk research
Description: Read old flood reports, news and water-level archives. Quick and cheap, but nobody from the riverbank has told you their story yet.

Title: Talk to riverside villages
Description: Ask residents how they learned about the last flood, who warned them and how much time they really needed to leave.

Title: Study the river
Description: Learn how fast the water rises, where official gauges already stand and which sensors survive ice, mud and frost.

Title: Full field study
Description: Interview residents, walk the banks with rescuers and analyse years of water-level data. Slow, but you will truly know your river.

Title: Bucket test
Description: One sensor above a bucket of water, sending numbers to your laptop. It proves the idea works. Nothing more.

Title: Manual alert service
Description: One basic sensor and a lot of handwork: every morning you check the river and send warnings to a village chat yourself.

Title: Bridge station prototype
Description: A real sensor on a real bridge, powered by a small solar panel. The data works. The app is just an ugly chart.

Title: Pilot network
Description: Three stations, a live map and SMS alerts for one village. Well built and ready to show, but it took serious time and effort.

Title: Shared purpose
Description: Your crew knows one sentence by heart: no family should learn about a flood from the water at their door.

Title: Values and roadmap
Description: Values like 'open by default' guide everyday decisions, and a roadmap shows the team what to build first.

Title: Values and mission
Description: Clear values for hard decisions and a mission that reminds everyone why the night shifts are worth it.

Title: Full team charter
Description: Mission, values, roadmap and clear roles for hardware, software and community work. Everyone knows why, how and what comes next.

Title: Water tank testing
Description: Test the stations in a water tank in your office. Fast and cheap, but a tank has no ice, no waves and no floating branches.

Title: Volunteer test group
Description: Thirty residents from two villages receive test alerts and tell you what is confusing, late or missing.

Title: Live river trial
Description: Put stations on the river and publish the data openly. Real conditions, real users and real bugs to fix quickly.

Title: Staged trial
Description: First the tank, then one village, then the whole district, each stage bigger than the last. Thorough and well prepared.

Title: Project website
Description: A simple site with the live river map, open data downloads and a sign-up form for alerts.

Title: Village chat groups
Description: Why build a website when every village already shares news in messenger groups? Go where people already are.

Title: Website and local media
Description: Local radio and TV spread the word fast, but people need a website to land on and sign up.

Title: Full awareness campaign
Description: Website, social media, school lessons, posters at bus stops and local volunteers. Everyone on the river should know about you.

Title: Single server
Description: One small server receives every reading and sends every alert. Cheap and simple. What could possibly go wrong?

Title: Cloud platform
Description: Run everything on a cloud service. It costs more, but it grows easily when the whole region signs up.

Title: Two servers with failover
Description: Two servers in different buildings. If one loses power in a storm, the other keeps sending alerts.

Title: Reliability team
Description: Hire engineers to run the system day and night with monitoring, backups and drills. A warning system must never sleep.

Title: Apply on your own
Description: Collect your licences, documentation and privacy policy, then submit the application on the DPG website yourself.

Title: Ask DPG experts for help
Description: Contact the DPG community and ask experienced reviewers to guide you through the application.

Title: Mention the SDG only
Description: Your project fights floods, so it clearly supports SDG 13. Surely that is enough for the application?

Title: Check all nine indicators
Description: Go through all nine DPG Standard indicators one by one, from open licences to privacy and do no harm, and prepare evidence for each.

Title: Pre-season campaign
Description: The whole team works on outreach before the spring melt. The technical side gets less attention.

Title: Launch day on the embankment
Description: A public launch by the river with a live demo stream. People will remember the day. Will they install the app?

Title: Essential release prep
Description: Not enough time for everything, so you fix the critical bugs and prepare a decent launch.

Title: Full release preparation
Description: Every station checked, every alert tested, every village briefed. It takes time, but spring will not wait for patches.

Title: Repair when broken
Description: Fix stations only when they stop working and answer messages when you can.

Title: Hotline and station checks
Description: A phone and email hotline for residents, plus regular trips to clean and recalibrate every station.

Title: Community stewardship
Description: Train local volunteers to look after stations, run yearly flood drills and keep the open data alive.

Title: Hire a service company
Description: Pay a contractor to handle repairs and support, so your team can focus on bringing the system to new rivers.
